newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran accuses U.S. of meddling in Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Iran accuses U.S. of meddling in Afghanistan.

text.p: Iran on Sunday accused the United States of meddling in Afghanistan's internal affairs, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
It quoted Iran's parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri as saying that "Iranian officials clearly see the the hands of the U.S. at work behind the Afghan issue."
He added that Afghanistan's problems can only be solved therough the cooperation of Afghan groups "without interferences of foreigners."
Nateq-Nouri was speaking in a meeting with the deputy chairman of Russia's State Duma lower house, IRNA said.
Iran said earlier on Sunday the takeover of the Afghan capital Kabul by a radical Islamic militia marked the beginning of a crisis, and urged Afghan leaders to stop fighting and start negotiations.
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Alaeddin Boroujerdi told IRNA his country was concerned about recent developments in neighbouring Afghanistan and would push for a peaceful resolution of the conflict.
"(It is) the start and not (the) end of crisis," Boroujerdi said, according to IRNA. "Naturally the Islamic Republic of Iran is concerned about the widening scope of the crisis."

Shi'ite Iran had supported the ousted Kabul government of President Burhannudin Rabbani and was hostile to the Sunni fundamentalist Taleban, which Iranian media allege are manipulated by Pakistan and the United States.
But Iranian officials have recently held talks with representatives of the Taleban militia.
Boroujerdi denied Rabbani's ouster was a setback for Iran's diplomacy, saying it was only interested in the restoration of peace and stability through negotiation.
"Iran rejects any activity outside this framework," he said, adding his country would remain active in Afghanistan's political scene and would continue efforts to promote peace.
